examples.name: Internal
examples.description: A route in the app. Without a target, Link renders target="_self".

examples.name: External
examples.description: target="_blank" adds the external-link icon, the hidden "(opens in a new tab)" text, and noopener noreferrer in rel on its own.

examples.name: Inline in a sentence
examples.description: emphasis="default" is the body weight for a link in running text; the text names the destination.
examples.jsx: Review the client profile before you continue.

examples.name: Name in a table cell
examples.description: The default strong emphasis is a heading weight for a name or first-column identifier; size="sm" sets heading-xxs for a dense table.

examples.name: Subtle
examples.description: appearance="subtle" is the quieter content color, for a light surface where the brand color would be too loud.

examples.name: Inverse on a dark surface
examples.description: appearance="inverse" is for a dark or bold surface only; on a light one it has almost no contrast.

examples.name: Translated new-tab text
examples.description: newTabLabel replaces the hidden text read after a new-tab link, for translation.
examples.jsx: <Link href="https://example.com" target="_blank" newTabLabel="(se abre en una pestaña nueva)">Guía de presentación</Link>

antiExamples.name: "Click here" link text
antiExamples.jsx: To review the client profile, click here.
antiExamples.reason: "Click here" says nothing about where the link goes when it's read out of context, as in a screen reader's list of links. Name the destination in the link text.

antiExamples.name: Adding your own new-tab icon and text
antiExamples.jsx:
<Link href="https://example.com" target="_blank">
  Court filing guidelines (opens in a new tab) <LinkExternalIcon />
</Link>
antiExamples.reason: With target="_blank", Link already adds the icon and hidden new-tab text, so yours shows twice and is read twice.

antiExamples.name: Link as a standalone call to action
antiExamples.reason: On its own, a Link reads as text rather than a control. Use Link Button for a call to action that stands on its own: <LinkButton href="/matters/new" appearance="primary">Start a new matter</LinkButton>.

antiExamples.name: Link for an action
antiExamples.reason: Link is for going somewhere. Saving, submitting a form, or opening a dialog is an action on this page: use Button.
